writeup.headline: Allegro rates Hold: strong growth and upbeat guidance offset by high absolute valuation and weak price trend.
writeup.thesis: Allegro scores 51, a Hold, because its strengths and weaknesses roughly cancel out. Growth is the strongest factor (77), with TTM revenue growth of 24.2% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 27.4% year on year, and growth sped up by 1.3 pp from the previous quarter. Against that, valuation scores just 23: in absolute terms the shares look expensive at 7.0x sales, 75.1x free cash flow and 143.7x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 3.7 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, although versus its own history the stock sits near the middle of its own history. The trend factor is also weak (30), with the price 49.2% below its 52-week high and shares 28.8 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. Quality is middling (51) given a thin 4.9% operating margin, while a solid balance sheet (70) and positive news on guidance and new AI data center products (61) help hold the score up.
key_risks: Valuation is high in absolute terms, at 143.7x EV/EBIT and 75.1x free cash flow, leaving little room if growth disappoints.
Operating margin of 4.9% is thin, so profits depend on the guided gross margin improvement to 51.5%–52.5% actually happening.
The share price is weak: 13.4% below its 200-day average and 49.2% below its 52-week high.
Ongoing dilution, with diluted share count up 1.7% year on year and stock-based compensation at 5.4% of revenue.
Mixed analyst views, including Wells Fargo cutting its target, plus general tariff and export-control exposure.
what_would_change: An upgrade to Buy needs 14 more points, most plausibly from a recovering price trend and better operating margins lifting the quality score.
A downgrade to Sell would follow a drop of 7 points, for example if revenue growth slows sharply and pulls the growth score down from 77.
Missing the new gross margin and EPS guidance, or negative news on guidance, would weigh on the news and quality factors.
A lower share price with steady free cash flow would improve the valuation score from its current 23.
